sentences.en: Classifications of Cultures.
sentences.zh: 文化的分类。
sentences.asr_text: Classifications of Cultures.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Good morning, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: Today we’ll look at culture or rather classifications of cultures.
sentences.zh: 今天我们来谈文化，更准确地说，是文化的分类。

sentences.en: Usually when we deal with different people, we deal with them as if we were all members of the same culture.
sentences.zh: 通常，与不同的人打交道时，我们会把对方当作与自己属于同一种文化的人。

sentences.en: However, it’s possible that people from different cultures have different assumptions about the world, regarding such important and basic ideas as time, personal space.
sentences.zh: 然而，来自不同文化的人，对于世界可能有不同的基本认识，其中就涉及时间、私人空间等重要而基础的观念。

sentences.en: And this is the view of Edward Hall.
sentences.zh: 这就是爱德华·霍尔的观点。

sentences.en: And Edward Hall is an anthropologist who spent a large part of his life studying American Indians, their culture, their language, but he was different from a lot of other anthropologists who just study one culture.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·霍尔是一位人类学家，他一生中的很大一部分时间都在研究美洲印第安人及其文化和语言，但他与许多只研究单一文化的人类学家不同。

sentences.en: He was interested in the relations between cultures, how cultures interact.
sentences.zh: 他关注的是不同文化之间的关系，以及文化如何相互作用。

sentences.en: What Hall believes is that cultures can be classified by placing them on a continuum, ranging from what he called high-context to low-context.
sentences.zh: 霍尔认为，可以把各种文化放到一条连续谱上加以分类，其范围从他所说的高语境文化一直延伸到低语境文化。

sentences.en: OK, what is a high-context culture?
sentences.zh: 好，那么什么是高语境文化呢？

w.m: phr.高语境文化；强语境文化

sentences.en: A high-context culture is a culture in which the context of the message or the action or an event carries a large part of its meaning and significance.
sentences.zh: 在高语境文化中，信息、行为或事件的很大一部分含义与意义，都由其所处的语境来承载。

sentences.en: What this means is that in a high-context culture more attention is paid to what’s happening in and around the message than to the message itself.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，在高语境文化中，人们更关注信息的相关背景和周围情境，而不是信息本身。

sentences.en: Now let me give you examples.
sentences.zh: 现在让我举些例子。

sentences.en: First in terms of personal space, generally speaking, in a high-context culture, because there’s greater dependency on group thinking, people lean towards heavier sensory involvement or closeness to people.
sentences.zh: 首先来看私人空间。一般来说，在高语境文化中，由于人们更依赖群体思维，他们倾向于更多的感官接触，或与他人保持更近的距离。

sentences.en: And they have less respect for privacy, for personal space.
sentences.zh: 他们对隐私、对私人空间的重视程度也较低。

sentences.en: If you go into that culture, people might stand closer when they’re talking to you.
sentences.zh: 如果你进入那样的文化环境，别人与你交谈时可能会站得更近。

sentences.en: They might touch more and if they’re jostled in a crowd, they won’t feel violated.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会有更多身体接触；即使在人群中被挤碰，也不会觉得受到了侵犯。

sentences.en: And also people from a high-context culture pay attention to body language.
sentences.zh: 此外，来自高语境文化的人会关注身体语言。

sentences.en: Because remember what I said, the definition of a high-context culture is that more attention is paid to the context of the message than to the message itself, and part of the context is body language.
sentences.zh: 因为，请记住我刚才说过的定义：高语境文化更关注信息的语境，而不是信息本身；身体语言也是语境的一部分。

sentences.en: Second, in terms of time, people in high-context cultures are considered to have what is called a polychronic attitude toward time.
sentences.zh: 其次，就时间而言，高语境文化中的人被认为持有所谓的多时制时间观。

w.m: adj.多时制的；允许多件事按各自节奏进行的

sentences.en: Here “poly” means multiple and “chronic” means time.
sentences.zh: 这里，“poly”表示“多个”，“chronic”表示“时间”。

sentences.en: What this means is that they believe people, things, events have their own time and there can’t be a standard system of time for everything.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，他们认为人、事物和事件各有各的时间节奏，不可能用一套标准的时间体系来统一规定一切。

sentences.en: What this leads them to believe is that you can’t emphasize punctuality.
sentences.zh: 由此，他们认为不应过分强调准时。

sentences.en: Things happen when they are supposed to happen.
sentences.zh: 事情会在它应当发生的时候发生。

sentences.en: So there’s a different attitude toward time.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一种不同的时间观。

sentences.en: There is no set standard of time.
sentences.zh: 时间没有固定的标准。

sentences.en: You can’t control time.
sentences.zh: 你无法控制时间。

sentences.en: Everything has its own sense of time.
sentences.zh: 万事万物都有自身的时间节奏。

sentences.en: So it’s a culture that pays little attention to time, to clock time.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种文化不太重视时间，不太重视钟表所显示的时间。

w.m: phr.钟表时间；按时钟计量的时间

sentences.en: Now, let’s move on to low-context culture.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们接着来看低语境文化。

sentences.en: A low-context culture is just the opposite.
sentences.zh: 低语境文化恰恰相反。

sentences.en: A low-context culture is one in which the message, the event or the action is a separate entity, having meaning unto itself, regardless of the surroundings or the context.
sentences.zh: 在低语境文化中，信息、事件或行为是独立的实体，自身就具有意义，不依赖周围的情境或语境。

sentences.en: That the message, the event, the action has meaning in itself.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，信息、事件和行为本身就有意义。

sentences.en: So what this means in a low-context culture is that people pay more attention to the event itself rather than to the context which surrounds the event or the message.
sentences.zh: 因此，在低语境文化中，人们更关注事件本身，而不是事件或信息所处的背景。

sentences.en: For example, in terms of personal space again.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们再以私人空间为例。

sentences.en: There’s more emphasis on individuality, so the concept of privacy is very very important, whereas before as I said, in a high-context culture they might not even be concerned with privacy or personal space.
sentences.zh: 这里更强调个体性，所以隐私的观念非常、非常重要；而正如我前面所说，在高语境文化中，人们可能甚至不太在意隐私或私人空间。

sentences.en: But in a low-context culture, there’s a feeling that we each have our own personal space.
sentences.zh: 但在低语境文化中，人们认为，每个人都有属于自己的私人空间。

sentences.en: If you get too close, if you don’t knock on doors before entering, that’s an invasion of privacy; people feel violated.
sentences.zh: 如果你靠得太近，或者进门之前不敲门，那就是侵犯隐私，人们会感到受到了侵犯。

sentences.en: There’s a respect and a desire for privacy, and you also see that people might pay less attention to body language because as I said the message is, the message is everything.
sentences.zh: 人们尊重并且渴望拥有隐私；你也会发现，他们可能不太关注身体语言，因为正如我所说，信息才是……信息才是一切。

sentences.en: They are not going to worry about all the details around it.
sentences.zh: 他们不会在意围绕信息的所有细节。

sentences.en: What you say is the important thing or what you do is the important thing.
sentences.zh: 重要的是你说了什么，或者你做了什么。

sentences.en: Another example of a low-context culture is people’s attitude towards time.
sentences.zh: 低语境文化的另一个例子，是人们对时间的态度。

sentences.en: In terms of time, I said before there was a polychronic sense of time in a high-context culture.
sentences.zh: 说到时间，我前面提过，高语境文化具有多时制的时间观。

sentences.en: What do you think there would be in a low-context culture?
sentences.zh: 你们认为，低语境文化会有怎样的时间观呢？

w.m: phr.低语境文化；弱语境文化

sentences.en: Monochronic! Right!
sentences.zh: 单时制！没错！

w.m: adj.单时制的；遵循统一时间表的

sentences.en: A monochronic sense of time and by that we mean that there is one time.
sentences.zh: 这是一种单时制的时间观，也就是说，只有一套统一的时间。

sentences.en: And that concept means that people in a low-context culture believe that there’s one standard of time and that should be for everything.
sentences.zh: 这种观念意味着，低语境文化中的人认为，存在一套统一的时间标准，而且万事都应遵守它。

sentences.en: And so I’m not willing to hear “Oh, the traffic was heavy. That’s why I am late.” or “Oh, I slept late.”
sentences.zh: 所以，我不愿听到“噢，交通太拥堵，所以我迟到了”，或者“噢，我睡过头了”这样的解释。

sentences.en: People in a low-context culture will be much more upset with lateness because they feel that everyone should follow the same time; there shouldn’t be all this flexibility with time and they expect punctuality.
sentences.zh: 低语境文化中的人会更难以接受迟到，因为他们认为，每个人都应遵守同一套时间，不应当对时间有这么大的弹性，而且他们要求准时。

sentences.en: And they look at time as almost a commodity that they use expressions like “use time”, “to waste time”, “to spend time” or “time is money”.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎把时间看作一种商品，因此会使用“利用时间”“浪费时间”“花费时间”，或者“时间就是金钱”这样的表达。

sentences.en: All of these expressions reinforce the concept that time is actually something you can hold onto.
sentences.zh: 所有这些表达，都强化了这样一种观念：时间实际上是可以把握在手中的东西。

sentences.en: So what this is all about is that Hall stresses that people need to be aware of these different assumptions or concepts about reality.
sentences.zh: 所以，归根结底，霍尔强调的是，人们需要意识到，不同文化对现实有着这些不同的预设或观念。

sentences.en: And he thinks that this has all kinds of relevance no matter what you’re doing, if you’re in business, negotiations, interpersonal relations, if you’re dealing with people from different cultures in any way, it’s going to affect every part of your life.
sentences.zh: 他认为，无论你从事什么，这些差异都与你密切相关：无论是商业活动、谈判，还是人际交往，只要你以任何方式与来自不同文化的人打交道，它就会影响你生活的各个方面。

sentences.en: In any multicultural situation, these assumptions need to be taken into account for successful interactions.
sentences.zh: 在任何多元文化的情境中，要实现成功的互动，都需要把这些预设考虑在内。

w.m: phr.把……考虑在内（本句为被动）

sentences.en: OK. Today, we’ve taken a brief look at Edward Hall’s view of culture, mainly his classification of high or low context culture with some examples.
sentences.zh: 好，今天我们简要了解了爱德华·霍尔的文化观，主要是他对高、低语境文化的分类，并看了一些例子。

sentences.en: Next week, we’ll look at some more examples of cultures on the continuum between high-context and low-context cultures.
sentences.zh: 下周，我们会进一步了解处于高语境与低语境文化连续谱上的其他文化实例。

sentences.en: Now you have Three minutes to check your work.
sentences.zh: 现在你有三分钟检查作答。
sentences.asr_text: Now you have Three minutes to check your work.

sentences.asr_text: Section B Interview

sentences.asr_text: The interview will be divided into two parts.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: At the end of each part, five questions will be asked about what was said.
sentences.zh: 每部分结束后，将就刚才所说的内容提出五个问题。
sentences.asr_text: At the end of each part, five questions will be asked about what was said.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.zh: 访谈和问题都只读一遍。
sentences.asr_text: Both the interview and the questions will be spoken once only.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: After each question, there will be a ten-second pause.
sentences.zh: 每个问题之后会有十秒钟的停顿。
sentences.asr_text: After each question, there will be a ten second pause.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C, and D, and mark the best answer to each question on Answer Sheet two.
sentences.zh: 请利用停顿时间阅读A、B、C、D四个选项，并在答题卡二上标出每题的最佳答案。
sentences.asr_text: During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C, and D, and mark the best answer to each question on Answer Sheet two.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: You have thirty seconds to preview the questions.
sentences.zh: 你有三十秒钟预览题目。
sentences.asr_text: You have thirty seconds to preview the questions.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Now listen to part one of the interview.
sentences.zh: 现在请听访谈的第一部分。
sentences.asr_text: Now listen to part one of the interview.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Questions 1 to 5 are based on part 1 of the interview.
sentences.zh: 第1至5题根据访谈的第一部分提问。
sentences.asr_text: Questions 1 to 5 are based on part 1 of the interview.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Good morning, Dr. Harley.
sentences.zh: 早上好，哈利博士。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for coming on our radio talk.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您来到我们的广播访谈节目。

sentences.en: We know that you are an applied linguist specializing in second language acquisition.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，您是一位专门研究第二语言习得的应用语言学家。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, today, urmm... we’ll look at this issue.
sentences.zh: 那么，今天，嗯……我们就来探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: Now, first, Dr. Harley, could you please tell us what is second language acquisition?
sentences.zh: 首先，哈利博士，能否请您告诉我们，什么是第二语言习得？
sentences.asr_ref: 核验/正文清理/2011-局部真词锚.json

sentences.en: Well, second language acquisition is “happens when a child or adult has already become competent at a language, and then, urmm... they attempt to learn another.”
sentences.zh: 嗯，第二语言习得是指这样的情况：儿童或成年人已经掌握了一种语言，然后，嗯……再尝试学习另一种语言。

sentences.en: OK, most people think, including me, it is difficult to learn another language.
sentences.zh: 好的。大多数人，包括我自己，都觉得学习另一种语言很难。

sentences.en: What are the reasons? Why is it so?
sentences.zh: 原因有哪些？为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Well, there are a number of reasons for this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有好几个原因。

sentences.en: Urmm... first, there have been research studies.
sentences.zh: 嗯……首先，已经有一些相关研究。

sentences.en: They have shown that some aspects of language learning, especially syntax, are more difficult beyond a certain age, say after around 12 years of age.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，语言学习的某些方面，尤其是句法，在超过一定年龄后，例如大约十二岁以后，会变得更难。

sentences.en: So, age plays an important role in language learning?
sentences.zh: 所以，年龄在语言学习中起着重要作用，是吗？

sentences.en: Yes. But that’s not the only reason.
sentences.zh: 是的。但这并不是唯一的原因。

sentences.en: Oh, is that so?
sentences.zh: 哦，是这样吗？

w.m: phr.是这样吗；表示追问或惊讶

sentences.en: Yes. For example, umm, time and interest.
sentences.zh: 是的。例如，嗯，时间和兴趣。

sentences.en: Old children and adults often have less time and motivation to learn a second language.
sentences.zh: 年龄较大的孩子和成年人，往往没有那么多时间和动力去学习第二语言。

sentences.en: Another is related to the similarities and differences between one’s mother tongue and a second language.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因与母语和第二语言之间的相似性及差异有关。

sentences.en: We find that learners will experience difficulty when their mother tongue and the second language they are learning differ.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当母语与正在学习的第二语言存在差异时，学习者就会遇到困难。

sentences.en: In general, the more idiosyncratic a feature is in a particular language, relative to other languages, the more difficult it will be to acquire.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，相比其他语言，某种语言的一个特征越独特，习得这个特征就越困难。

sentences.en: Perhaps this is the key issue.
sentences.zh: 也许这正是关键所在。

sentences.en: Differences between languages cause language learning problems.
sentences.zh: 语言之间的差异会导致语言学习困难。

sentences.en: Well, this may be one of the issues here, but this cannot be the whole story, as not all differences between languages cause difficulty.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这也许是其中的一个问题，但事情并不完全如此，因为并非语言之间的所有差异都会造成困难。
sentences.asr_ref: 核验/正文清理/2011-局部真词锚.json

sentences.en: Let me give you an example.
sentences.zh: 让我举个例子。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Research has found that many errors by Czech speakers learning English were made on syntactic constructions in which the two languages do not differ.
sentences.zh: 研究发现，母语为捷克语的人学习英语时，许多错误恰恰出现在两种语言没有差异的句法结构上。

sentences.en: Oh, really? The picture is more complicated than we’ve imagined.
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？情况比我们想象的还要复杂。

sentences.en: Definitely yes.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Each language learning situation is different.
sentences.zh: 每一种语言学习情境都不同。

sentences.en: So reasons vary a lot from case to case.
sentences.zh: 所以，原因会因具体情况而大不相同。

w.m: phr.视具体情况而定；因情况而异

sentences.en: Now, Dr. Harley. Since learning a second language is a difficult process, you know, in one way or another, are there any methods, so far, effective methods to teach a second language?
sentences.zh: 那么，哈利博士，既然学习第二语言是一个艰难的过程，或多或少都会遇到困难，那么到目前为止，有没有什么方法，有效的方法，来教授第二语言？

w.m: phr.以某种方式；在某种程度上

sentences.en: There again. No method is absolutely effective in all situations.
sentences.zh: 这里也是一样。没有一种方法在所有情境下都绝对有效。

sentences.en: Some may prove effective, others may not.
sentences.zh: 有些方法可能有效，有些则可能无效。

sentences.en: I mean, all depending on specific conditions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一切都取决于具体条件。

sentences.en: But generally speaking, there are a number of methods that have been used to teach a second language.
sentences.zh: 不过，一般来说，已经有若干种方法被用于第二语言教学。

sentences.en: Could you mention a few?
sentences.zh: 您能举出几种吗？

sentences.en: For instance, there is the traditional method.
sentences.zh: 例如，有传统教学法。

sentences.en: This method is based on translation from one language to another and it emphasizes grammar teaching.
sentences.zh: 这种方法以两种语言之间的翻译为基础，并强调语法教学。

sentences.en: Mm...
And then you have direct methods, which focuses on conversational skills and all teaching must be carried out in the second language.
sentences.zh: 然后还有直接教学法，它着重培养会话技能，而且全部教学都必须使用第二语言进行。

sentences.en: Oh, I see. Any other methods?
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。还有其他方法吗？

sentences.en: Yes. For example, the audiolingual method.
sentences.zh: 有的。例如，听说法。

sentences.en: This method emphasizes speaking and listening before reading and writing.
sentences.zh: 这种方法强调先进行说和听的训练，再进行读写训练。

sentences.en: How interesting!
sentences.zh: 真有意思！

sentences.en: Then you have the immersion method.
sentences.zh: 然后还有沉浸式教学法。

sentences.en: This method teaches learners exclusively through the medium of the second language.
sentences.zh: 这种方法完全以第二语言为媒介来教授学习者。

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 怎么进行呢？

w.m: 交际用语.怎么进行呢；请求进一步解释

sentences.en: Well, it simply means that you cannot speak mother tongue.
sentences.zh: 嗯，简单来说，就是不能说母语。
sentences.asr_ref: 核验/正文清理/2011-局部真词锚.json

sentences.en: Everything must be done in the language you are learning.
sentences.zh: 所有事情都必须用你正在学习的语言来完成。

sentences.en: To me, the most natural method of learning a new language is what I call submersion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，学习一门新语言最自然的方式，是我所说的“完全置身其中”。

w.m: n.浸入；此处指完全置身目标语环境

sentences.en: That is, to go to that country and be surrounded exclusively by speakers of that language.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，去到那个国家，周围接触到的全是说那种语言的人。

sentences.en: This is the end of part one of the interview.
sentences.zh: 访谈的第一部分到此结束。
sentences.asr_text: This is the end of part one of the interview.

sentences.en: Now, listen to part two of the interview.
sentences.zh: 现在请听访谈的第二部分。
sentences.asr_text: Now, listen to part two of the interview.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Questions 6 to 10 are based on part 2 of the interview.
sentences.zh: 第6至10题根据访谈的第二部分提问。
sentences.asr_text: Questions 6 to 10 are based on part 2 of the interview.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Dr. Harley, for introducing some of the language teaching methods.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您，哈利博士，为我们介绍了几种语言教学方法。

sentences.en: Now let’s move on to something a bit theoretical.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们来谈一些稍微偏理论的话题。

sentences.en: Since second language acquisition and teaching are a fascinating area for researchers, are there any theories to explain second language acquisition?
sentences.zh: 既然第二语言习得及其教学是一个令研究者着迷的领域，那么有没有什么理论可以解释第二语言习得呢？

w.m: adj.极有吸引力的；令人着迷的

sentences.en: Yes, many theories and models have been put forward by researchers so far.
sentences.zh: 有的。到目前为止，研究者已经提出了许多理论和模型。

sentences.en: Today, I’d like to mention the five hypotheses proposed by Stephen Krashen.
sentences.zh: 今天，我想介绍斯蒂芬·克拉申提出的五个假说。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The five hypotheses form what he calls the monitor model of second language learning.
sentences.zh: 这五个假说构成了他所说的第二语言学习监控模型。

sentences.en: What does it mean?
sentences.zh: 这是什么意思呢？

w.m: 交际用语.这是什么意思；请求解释

sentences.en: OK. The first hypothesis is the acquisition and learning distinction hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 好的。第一个假说是习得与学习区分假说。

sentences.en: According to Krashen, children acquire their first language largely unconsciously and automatically, but adults could only learn a second language consciously and effortfully.
sentences.zh: 克拉申认为，儿童主要是在无意识、自然而然的过程中习得母语，而成年人只能有意识地、付出努力地学习第二语言。

w.m: adv.费力地；需要付出努力地

sentences.en: And adults could indeed acquire the second language, at least in part.
sentences.zh: 不过，成年人确实也能够习得第二语言，至少在一定程度上是这样。

w.m: phr.至少在一定程度上；至少部分地

sentences.en: Right. Then what’s his second hypothesis?
sentences.zh: 好的。那么，他的第二个假说是什么？
sentences.asr_ref: 核验/正文清理/2011-局部真词锚.json

sentences.en: His second hypothesis is the natural order in acquisition hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 他的第二个假说是习得自然顺序假说。

sentences.en: Basically, he means that the order in which learners acquire syntactic rules is the same in both languages.
sentences.zh: 基本意思是，学习者在两种语言中习得句法规则的顺序是相同的。

sentences.en: Oh, that’s something really new to me.
sentences.zh: 哦，这对我来说真是个全新的认识。

sentences.en: The third hypothesis is the monitor hypothesis, which is central to his theory.
sentences.zh: 第三个假说是监控假说，它是他整个理论的核心。

sentences.en: Here again, we come across the distinction between acquisition and learning.
sentences.zh: 这里，我们再次遇到了习得与学习之间的区别。

sentences.en: According to this hypothesis, the acquisition processes create sentences in the second language, right?
sentences.zh: 根据这个假说，习得过程负责生成第二语言的句子，对吧？

sentences.en: But learning enables the development of a monitoring process to check and edit this output.
sentences.zh: 而学习则能够形成一个监控过程，用来检查并修改这些语言输出。

sentences.en: The monitor uses knowledge of the rules.
sentences.zh: 这个监控机制运用的是语言规则方面的知识。

sentences.en: That’s why, as I said just now, learning is a conscious process.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我刚才所说，学习是一个有意识的过程。

sentences.en: This means, in learning, you use knowledge of the language to make sure what you say or write is correct.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，在学习过程中，你会运用语言知识，确保自己所说或所写的内容正确。

sentences.en: Is that so?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

w.m: 交际用语.是这样吗；请求确认

sentences.en: Yes. His fourth hypothesis is the comprehensible input hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 是的。他的第四个假说是可理解输入假说。

sentences.en: In order to move from one stage to the next, the learner must understand the meaning and the form of the input.
sentences.zh: 学习者要从一个阶段进步到下一个阶段，就必须理解输入内容的意义和形式。

w.m: n.输入；接收到的语言材料

sentences.en: This emphasizes the role of comprehension.
sentences.zh: 这强调了理解所起的作用。

sentences.en: And finally, the active filter hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 最后，是情感过滤假说。

w.m: n.过滤器；此处指影响语言习得的过滤机制

sentences.en: This suggests attitude and emotional factors are also important in second language acquisition.
sentences.zh: 这一假说认为，态度和情感因素在第二语言习得中也很重要。

sentences.en: I guess Krashen’s model has provided a useful framework for second language learning.
sentences.zh: 我想，克拉申的模型为第二语言学习提供了一个有用的框架。

sentences.en: Yes, it indeed has and it has also proved to be one of the most influential theoretical approaches to teaching a second language.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此，而且它也已被证明是第二语言教学中最有影响力的理论路径之一。
sentences.asr_ref: 核验/正文清理/2011-局部真词锚.json

sentences.en: OK, Dr. Harley. Thank you once again for talking to us about second language acquisition.
sentences.zh: 好的，哈利博士。再次感谢您与我们探讨第二语言习得。

sentences.en: Pleasure.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

w.m: 交际用语.我的荣幸；不客气
